edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Sed ut diximus, eadem dementia est, cum confitentur quidem, nihil Apostolos ignorasse, nec diversa inter se praedicasse; non tamen omnia volunt illos omnibus revelasse: quaedam enim palam, et universis; quaedam secreto, et paucis demandasse: quia et hoc verbo usus est Paulus ad Timotheum: O Timothee, depositum custodi. Et rursum: Bonum depositum serva. Quod hoc depositum est tacitum, ut alteri doctrinae deputetur? An illius denuntiationis, de qua ait: Hanc denuntiationem commendo apud te, fili Timothee. Item illius praecepti, de quo ait: Denuntio tibi ante Deum, qui vivificat omnia, et Jesum Christum, qui testatus est sub Pontio Pilato bonam confessionem, custodias praeceptum Quod autem praeceptum, et quae denuntiatio? Ex supra et infra scriptis intelligetur non nescio quid subostendi hoc dicto de remotiore doctrina, sed potius inculcari de non admittenda alia praeter eam, quam audierat ab ipso, et, puto, palam. Coram multis, inquit, testibus. Quos multos testes si nolunt Ecclesiam intelligi, nihil interest, quando nihil tacitum fuerit, quod sub multis testibus proferebatur. Sed nec quia voluit illum haec fidelibus hominibus demandare, qui idonei sint et alios docere id quoque ad argumentum occulti alicujus Evangelii interpretandum est. Nam cum dicit, haec, de eis dicit, de quibus in praesenti scribebat; de occultis autem, ut de absentibus apud conscientiam, non haec, sed illa dixisset.
pass_a_gloss: But as we have said, it is the same foolishness when they confess that the Apostles indeed knew nothing, and did not preach different things among themselves; yet they do not want them to have revealed all things to all people: for some things they entrusted openly and to all, but some things secretly and to a few; because Paul also used this word to Timothy: O Timothy, guard the deposit. And again: Keep the good deposit. What is this deposit, silent, so that it may be assigned to another doctrine? Or is it of that announcement, about which he says: I commend this announcement to you, son Timothy. Likewise of that precept, about which he says: I denounce to you before God, who gives life to all, and Jesus Christ, who testified a good confession under Pontius Pilate, guard the precept. But what precept, and what announcement? It will be understood from the writings above and below, I do not know what I have hinted at with this statement about a more remote doctrine, but rather that it is inculcated not to admit another besides that which he heard from him, and, I think, openly. Before many witnesses, he says. If they do not want the Church to be understood as many witnesses, it does not matter, since nothing was silent that was brought forth before many witnesses. But neither is it because he wanted to entrust these things to faithful men, who are suitable to teach others, is this also to be interpreted as an argument for some hidden Gospel. For when he says these things, he says them about those things which he was writing about at the present time; but about hidden things, as about those absent from conscience, he would not have said these things, but those things.

choices.why: accurate translation of the Latin term

pass_b_english: As I said, it is the same foolishness when they admit that the Apostles knew nothing and did not preach contradictory things among themselves, yet they refuse to accept that the Apostles revealed everything to everyone. They claim some things were entrusted openly to all, others secretly to a few, because Paul also used this language with Timothy: "Timothy, guard the deposit" (1 Timothy 6:20). And again: "Guard the good deposit" (1 Timothy 6:20). What is this deposit, kept silent, so that it might be assigned to some other doctrine? Or does it refer to that charge, about which he says: "I entrust this charge to you, my son Timothy" (1 Timothy 1:18)? Likewise, does it refer to that command, about which he says: "I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate, to keep the commandment" (1 Timothy 6:13)? But what command, and what charge? It will be understood from the passages above and below. I am not hinting at some obscure doctrine with this statement; rather, the point is to inculcate that no teaching other than what Timothy heard from Paul—and, I think, publicly—is to be admitted. "Before many witnesses," he says. If they refuse to understand the Church as those many witnesses, it makes no difference, since nothing was kept secret that was brought forward before many witnesses. Nor does the fact that he wanted to entrust these things to faithful men who are competent to teach others serve as an argument for some hidden Gospel. For when he says "these things," he means the things he was writing about at that moment; about hidden things, as about things absent from the conscience, he would not have said "these things," but "those things."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required inline scripture citations (1 Timothy 6:20, 1 Timothy 1:18, 1 Timothy 6:13) which correspond to the Latin clauses. Pass A and B are consistent with the source. The distinction between 'these things' (haec) and 'those things' (illa) at the end of the paragraph is preserved.
